questions.q: Why is IAM described as a global service?
options: An IAM user or role is available account-wide and isn't scoped to any single Region
Because it can only be accessed from the us-east-1 Region
Because every AWS account shares the exact same IAM users
Because IAM is only available to accounts inside an AWS Organization
questions.explain: Unlike most AWS services, IAM identities aren't tied to a specific Region — they apply across the whole account.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an IAM user and an IAM role?
options: A user has long-term credentials; a role has no long-term credentials and is temporarily assumed instead
A role can only be used by IAM users, never by AWS services
A user can only be a person, while a role can only be a group of people
There is no functional difference between the two
questions.explain: Roles are temporary and assumed on demand, which is exactly what makes them safer for services than long-lived user credentials.

options: A JSON document that specifies which actions are allowed or denied, on which resources, under what conditions
A billing report showing IAM-related costs
A list of every IAM user in the account, with no permission data
A setting that controls which Region an account can operate in
questions.explain: Policies are the actual permission documents attached to users, groups, or roles that IAM evaluates on each request.

questions.q: Why does a Lambda function typically get an execution role instead of an IAM user's access keys?
options: A role gives it temporary, auto-rotated credentials with no long-lived secret sitting in code that could leak
Execution roles are required by AWS billing rules for all Lambda functions
Access keys cannot technically be used by any AWS service, only by humans
Roles are free while access keys incur an additional charge
questions.explain: This is exactly why roles are the recommended pattern for service-to-service access — no hardcoded, long-lived credential to leak.

questions.q: What does the principle of least privilege mean in IAM?
options: Granting only the minimum permissions actually needed to do a job, not broad access 'just in case'
Giving every identity full administrator access by default
Only applying permissions to IAM groups, never to individual users or roles
Limiting an AWS account to a maximum of five IAM policies
questions.explain: Least privilege is IAM's organizing idea: scope permissions tightly to what's actually required.
